what_was_missing: Seven step groups. (1) PERST# pin control with ADT timing: t-refclk-to-perst 100 us and perst-to-config 100 ms. (2) The lane reference clock handshake in the port-0 lane bank (ADT reg[8]): config access, refclk 0/1 request and ack, refclk enable, then port refclk. (3) Port ready after the PERST cycle, and clock gating. (4) Port interrupt mask/clear. (5) MSI doorbell from ADT 0xfffff000, base 0, log2 vectors. (6) RID-to-SID table probe, clear and program. (7) LTSSM start and a bounded link-up wait.
what_it_is: linkup.c/linkup.h: apl_link_port0, original pure-C Darwin code with 21 steps, run once after a completed apb_bringup_port0 through the same apb_io callbacks plus an apl_pins pair. Writes go only to a whitelist. Waits are bounded, there are no retries, and a dirty record is refused. LINKUP.md maps every Linux step to slice 2, this stage or 'not taken'.
gate: Lane-bank writes (shared PHY window) and the PERST#/power-enable pin calls (shared GPIO/SMC blocks) exist only under APB_FAKE_REGISTER_FILE, which every KERNEL build refuses with #error. The stage also refuses to start without a completed slice-2 record that shows shared writes and no gated writes, and a bundle can never produce one. With a forged record, its first write is the gated PERST# call, so it stops with zero writes. No adapter code calls it.

checks.host: test_linkup.py exit 0. ASan/UBSan fake mode runs slice 2 and then this stage on one simulated register file, covering order, timings, every timeout, faults, table sizes, MSI variants and power-enable. Gated mode refuses a real gated slice-2 record and stops a forged one at PERST# with 0 writes and 0 pin calls. Gate proofs pass, 17 of 17 mutants are caught, and a plan built from the saved J293 ADT (5f2ad465...) passes. Slice-1 and slice-2 runners still pass.
checks.sdk_bundle: build-linkup-gate.nix exit 0. It builds the slice-1 bundle plus bringup.c and linkup.c as kernel code (ARM64 MH_BUNDLE, executable 131743 B, sha256 9352a7d474484c689951fa567b4262432c369e49907b0cd7077aeaa37682b0b3). There are no warnings from either engine and no new imports.
checks.binary: check_linkup_bundle.py exit 0. The slice-2 checks pass unchanged. apl_shared_writes_compiled is mov w0,#0; ret. Kernel pin() contains no call. The shared branch of wr() contains no call. The only indirect calls are read, delay and the port-path write. Nothing refers to either stage's entry. The bundle text matches linkup.c.o.

deliberate_differences: Refuses an already-up link instead of skipping. Checks APPCLK instead of re-setting it, so PERST# is the first write. Polls link-up with port interrupts left masked. Programs and reads back table entries before training, with stream IDs of 4 bits. MSI base is always 0. Timings come from the ADT with PCIe floors.
open: A Darwin GPIO service for PERST# (/arm-io/gpio pin 152). Whether the BCM4378 needs a power rail (the ADT declares no power-enable). DART stream IDs. An IOKit apb_io backend. The slice-2 scope review of the shared PHY and PMGR writes.
